bio: Scarborough rapper Grimace Love is a veteran of Toronto’s underground hip-hop scene and a longtime member of the Monolith collective. His solo work carries the rugged boom-bap sound associated with the crew while giving more room to his raspy delivery, storytelling and personal writing.

Vancouver-born Claire Boucher developed Grimes after moving to Montréal and becoming immersed in the city's DIY electronic scene. Early releases Geidi Primes and Halfaxa established a homemade, otherworldly aesthetic, but Visions was the international breakthrough. Built largely through self-directed production, the album fused electronic music, dream pop, dance rhythms and layered vocals into songs such as "Oblivion" and "Genesis," placing Boucher among the most distinctive Canadian artists to emerge from the early-2010s independent electronic underground.

Art Angels dramatically expanded the sound. Written and recorded as a solo production project, it brought more live instrumentation, brighter pop structures and sharper contrasts to songs including "Flesh Without Blood" and "Kill V. Maim." Miss Anthropocene then turned climate anxiety and human extinction into a darker conceptual frame. Across these records, Grimes also treated visual art, video, character design and technology as extensions of the music rather than secondary promotional elements, making the project as much about world-building as conventional singer-songwriter identity.

Grimes matters in Canadian music because the project helped collapse boundaries between experimental electronic production and internet-era pop. Boucher's insistence on producing and engineering much of her own work also challenged assumptions about authorship around female electronic artists. Her later interest in virtual performers, synthetic voices and AI has been divisive, but it follows a long-running tendency in the project: using new tools, imagined identities and digital culture as material for pop experimentation rather than treating technology as separate from the art.

Gritfall is a Toronto hip-hop artist associated with the city's current underground rap scene. The catalogue includes solo material and collaborations with artists including Shadee, Forest N/A and Rico Blox. Northern Dial carries Gritfall as part of its emerging Canadian hip-hop coverage.
Indian-born Canadian rapper and singer Gurinder Gill is a Victoria-rooted Punjabi artist whose global catalogue blends Punjabi vocals with hip-hop, R&B, pop rap and trap.

Gutta192 is a Quebec rapper working within the province's contemporary francophone hip-hop scene. His releases are catalogued by MUSIQC as part of Quebec rap, placing him within the current generation of independent Canadian francophone artists. Northern Dial carries Gutta192 as part of its Quebec hip-hop catalogue.

Toronto-born Haley Smalls has built one of the more sustained independent R&B catalogues in Canada by combining expressive vocals, candid songwriting and unusually hands-on control over her recordings. Classically trained as a singer, she was recording in professional studios from a young age and later taught herself audio engineering, a skill that became central to her independence. Rather than separating performance from production, Smalls developed as an artist, songwriter and engineer at the same time, giving her work a consistency that has survived multiple changes in the R&B landscape.

Her first major run of projects began with the 2015 mixtapes This Is Me and Imagination and continued through The Cure, The Cure II, Heart of Gold and 2019's Summer Nights. Longtime collaborator Megaman helped shape a sound that balances contemporary R&B polish with a softer, more intimate vocal approach. A 2014 moment in which Beyoncé shared Smalls' cover of "Pretty Hurts" brought a burst of international attention, but Smalls ultimately doubled down on an independent path instead of treating that exposure as a route into the label system.

That long-game approach has continued through later releases including The Cure III, Timelines, 333, The Cure IV and 2025's Matches. By 2026, Smalls was touring internationally while maintaining the direct-to-fan model that had defined her career. Her significance in Canadian R&B comes less from one crossover hit than from durability and control: she has built a sizeable catalogue, developed technical authority over her own sound and shown how an independent Toronto artist can sustain audience growth without relying on a single industry breakthrough.

Halifax singer-songwriter Haliey Smith is an African Nova Scotian R&B and soul artist with deep roots in the province's music community. A longtime session and background vocalist, she has performed with artists including David Myles and Joel Plaskett, appeared with Symphony Nova Scotia and stepped into a solo career with releases including Fall In Love.

Hampton the Hampster is the fictional Canadian novelty-dance act spun out of Deidre LaCarte’s pioneering Hampster Dance website. The musical project was developed with Toronto production team The Boomtang Boys, whose 2000 single The Hampsterdance Song became a Canadian chart-topper before expanding into albums and follow-up singles.

Harley G is a Canadian hip-hop artist and Oshawa figure whose recording catalogue includes the 2024 single 'I Wont Change' with Snow and Young Stitch, released through Shark Tank Recordings. The performing identity connects directly to Harley Davidson Guindon, known locally through the Harley G's brand in Oshawa and documented as having been born in Oshawa, Ontario. His music activity is rooted in the Durham Region scene, including Ontario tour appearances alongside Merkules, Icarus and Young Stitch.
Toronto electronic producer Harrison Robinson makes melodic, jazz- and R&B-informed electronic music and has become a distinctive voice in Canada's beat and dance-music scenes.

Ottawa-raised, Toronto-based rapper Harvey Stripes is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose independent career has included national touring and collaborations with artists from both Canadian and U.S. rap scenes.

Hatfield is a Canadian rapper and singer-songwriter from Weymouth, Nova Scotia, formerly known as Khaki Ka$h and Just Q. His music moves between golden-era boom bap, melodic rap and alternative influences, reflecting a long-running connection to Nova Scotia's independent hip-hop community. Northern Dial carries Hatfield as part of its Atlantic Canadian rap catalogue.

Hawksley Workman built one of the more singular long careers in Canadian singer-songwriter music by treating genre as something to move through rather than settle into. Born in Huntsville, Ontario, he emerged at the end of the 1990s as a multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and producer with the self-produced debut For Him and the Girls. Its theatrical vocals, cabaret-pop eccentricity and songs such as "Safe and Sound" quickly established an artistic persona far removed from the post-grunge rock dominating Canadian radio. He pushed that approach further on (Last Night We Were) The Delicious Wolves, whose combination of glam-rock swagger, piano balladry and pop craft brought broader attention and helped earn Workman JUNO recognition in the early 2000s.

Rather than narrowing his sound after that breakthrough, Workman kept expanding an unusually prolific catalogue. Lover/Fighter in 2003 produced songs such as "Smoke Baby" and "We Will Still Need a Song" and contributed to a 2004 JUNO nomination for Songwriter of the Year. He moved through quieter seasonal writing on Almost a Full Moon, the stripped-back Treeful of Starling, rock records, theatrical projects and later albums including Median Age Wasteland and Less Rage More Tears. Alongside his own releases, Workman's reputation as a producer and collaborator became another important part of his career, placing him inside a wider Canadian indie and singer-songwriter network rather than only his own discography.

Workman's longevity is central to why he matters. His official biography describes a catalogue of 17 solo records and more than a thousand performances, with sustained audiences not only across Canada but in Europe, the United Kingdom and Australia. Decades after his debut, he continues to tour nationally and release new music, including the 2025 Fly Like an Ego EP. That durability makes him difficult to reduce to any single early hit or genre label: Workman helped demonstrate that a deliberately theatrical, eccentric Canadian songwriter could build a durable international career while moving between cabaret, folk, glam, pop and rock on his own terms.

Headnodz is a Toronto hip-hop production identity associated with producers Nick Holder and Kaje and the city's Treehouse Records circle. The project produced material for Canadian underground artists including Citizen Kane, Mathematik, Reign and Dub Ill during Treehouse's independent rap run. Northern Dial carries Headnodz as part of its foundational Toronto producer catalogue.

Headstones emerged from Kingston, Ontario, with frontman Hugh Dillon's confrontational delivery giving the band a harder, punk-informed edge than much of Canada's early-1990s alternative-rock boom. After signing with MCA, the group broke nationally with the 1993 debut Picture of Health, whose songs included "Cemetery" and "When Something Stands for Nothing." The album eventually went platinum in Canada, establishing Headstones as both a forceful live act and a dependable presence on Canadian rock radio.

The 1995 follow-up Teeth and Tissue went gold and earned a JUNO nomination for Best Rock Album, while the next phase of the catalogue produced further radio staples and reinforced the band's mix of hard-rock weight, punk abrasion and dark humour. Dillon's work in films such as Dance Me Outside and Hard Core Logo also gave the group's music a broader cultural context, linking Headstones to a distinctly Canadian strain of rough-edged independent film and rock culture during the same period.

Headstones disbanded in 2003, then reunited in 2011 and resumed recording and touring rather than treating the comeback as a one-off nostalgia exercise. Love + Fury arrived in 2013 and earned another JUNO nomination for Rock Album of the Year, beginning a sustained second chapter that carried the band well beyond its original 1990s run. That durability is part of the Headstones story: a Kingston-born group whose abrasive identity, live intensity and national catalogue remained recognizable enough to support an active career decades after Picture of Health first broke through.
Abbotsford, British Columbia group Hedley was a Canadian pop-rock band active from 2003 to 2018, with a commercially successful catalogue spanning pop-punk and polished mainstream rock.

Hellbent is a Canadian dance and electronic project led by producer Vince 'Vinny Mac' Maria and vocalist-songwriter Rachelle Loren. The group built national and international radio momentum with Fast Car and later continued through club-oriented singles and remixes on Intense Records. The Ryder Remix of Fast Car is the Hellbent recording represented in the Northern Dial library.

St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador band Hey Rosetta! was a Canadian indie-rock ensemble led by Tim Baker, known for emotionally expansive songs built around rock instrumentation, strings and piano.

HeyBombay, also known as Bombay, is a Qatar-born music producer residing in Toronto, Canada. Working across hip-hop, R&B, neo-soul and beat music, he became a key collaborator of Toronto artist Ice Tha One, producing her MONSTAR material and later sharing artist billing on the deluxe edition. Their Dance Like Me collaboration with Truss and Junia-T is HeyBombay's Northern Dial library credit.

Hip Club Groove is a Nova Scotia hip-hop group that emerged from Truro before becoming part of Halifax's early-1990s rap and indie ecosystem. The best-known lineup paired MCs Cheklove Shakil and Derek MacKenzie with DJ Moves. Their 1993 Cool Beans EP led to Trailer Park Hip Hop on Sloan's murderecords in 1994, and the group played across genre lines at a moment when Halifax was drawing national attention for its independent music scene. Hip Club Groove later released Land of the Lost in 1996 before going quiet. In 2026, Cheklove, MacKenzie and Moves reunited for Dead Words, their first new song in 30 years, recorded for Hand'Solo Records' Bassments of Badmen 4 compilation.

Québec City singer, songwriter and producer Hubert Lenoir broke through nationally with the 2018 solo debut Darlène, a theatrical glam-rock album structured around a fictional romantic narrative. Its flamboyant presentation and refusal to separate rock spectacle from francophone chanson made Lenoir an unusually visible figure in Québec pop culture, attracting both intense praise and backlash. Darlène was shortlisted for the 2018 Polaris Music Prize, placing the album alongside some of the year's most critically recognized Canadian releases.

Rather than repeating that record's sound, Lenoir used the reaction around his debut as fuel for PICTURA DE IPSE : Musique directe. Released in 2021, the second album moved through synth-pop, experimental rock, noise and deliberately exposed autobiographical material, with Lenoir describing the album itself as his primary artistic medium rather than treating it as a collection of singles. Polaris again shortlisted him in 2022, making the project a second nationally recognized statement rather than a one-album provocation.

Lenoir matters because his career reopened an old Québec pop tension in a contemporary form: how far a francophone artist can push image, sexuality, genre and public persona while still operating inside mainstream cultural conversation. His work travels beyond Québec without sanding away its language or local references, and the two Polaris shortlist appearances show that the musical ambition underneath the controversy has had sustained critical weight across Canada.

HXGO is a Canadian music artist from Ottawa, Ontario. His catalogue spans hip-hop and alternative-leaning releases including the 2021 Sam-r collaboration 'Good Time,' where HXGO is credited as the featured artist and composer Hugo Marín, alongside solo releases such as 'Timeless,' 'Ukulele' and 'Talkaboutit.' Independent creative-project documentation for HXGO's 2020 single 'Man on the Moon' explicitly identifies him as a Canadian music artist from Ottawa, providing direct artist-level location evidence for the HXGO identity.

I Mother Earth formed in Toronto at the beginning of the 1990s around brothers Jagori and Christian Tanna, developing a rock sound that drew as readily from funk, progressive rock and percussion-heavy fusion as it did from the alternative boom around them. Their 1993 debut Dig, fronted by Edwin, introduced that combination through long, groove-oriented arrangements and strong musicianship. The group stood apart from simpler post-grunge formulas by making rhythmic complexity and instrumental interplay central to its identity.

The 1996 follow-up Scenery and Fish became the band's commercial high point, reaching double-platinum status in Canada and producing enduring rock-radio songs such as "One More Astronaut," "Another Sunday" and "Used to Be Alright." Edwin left after that period and Brian Byrne became the new vocalist for Blue Green Orange and The Quicksilver Meat Dream. The lineup change altered the vocal character without erasing the Tanna brothers' dense, groove-driven approach.

After going inactive in the early 2000s, I Mother Earth reunited in 2012 and later performed again with Edwin, reconnecting the most familiar lineup with audiences that had kept Scenery and Fish in Canadian rock circulation. The band's significance is partly technical and partly historical: I Mother Earth brought progressive and fusion-minded playing into a mainstream 1990s Canadian rock setting, giving the era a sound that was heavier and more rhythmically adventurous than the post-grunge label usually suggests.

I.R.S. is an alternate library credit for the Canadian Scarborough hip-hop trio IRS, made up of Korry Deez, Black Cat and producer T.R.A.C.K.S. The Monolith-affiliated group released the Juno-nominated Welcome to Planet IRS and also appeared on The Real Frequency's Toronto compilation The New North.

iBXRHM is a Toronto R&B artist whose music blends contemporary soul, melodic hip-hop and atmospheric production. The artist, also known as Ibrahim Ahmed, is based in Toronto and has developed an independent catalogue within the city's emerging R&B scene. Northern Dial carries iBXRHM as part of its contemporary Canadian R&B catalogue.

Angela Musceo, better known as Ice Tha One, is a Canadian singer, songwriter and emcee rooted in Toronto's east end. Moving from Canada's east coast to Toronto while young, she developed a genre-fluid style spanning hip-hop, R&B, soul and jazz and has built a catalogue around projects including In The Paint, MONSTAR and MONSTAR DELUXE while remaining active in community arts and mentorship.

Canadian-Punjabi singer Inderpal Moga has become a prominent voice in contemporary Punjabi music through a run of melodic street records and collaborations with artists including Chani Nattan, AR Paisley, Dr Zeus and Jazzy B. His catalogue bridges Punjabi music with the sound and perspective of the Canadian diaspora.

Ironside is a Toronto hip-hop artist associated with Ghetto Concept and the 7Bills scene. He appeared alongside major Canadian rappers on Ghetto Concept's Still Too Much and is part of the documented network around Toronto's late-1990s and early-2000s underground rap movement. Northern Dial carries Ironside as part of its archival Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

IRS, short for Instinctive Reaction to Struggle, was a Canadian hip-hop trio from Scarborough made up of MCs Korry Deez and Black Cat with DJ-producer T.R.A.C.K.S. Emerging from the larger Monolith collective, the group signed with Universal Music Canada and released the Juno-nominated 2003 album Welcome to Planet IRS, home to the Toronto anthem T-Dot Anthem.

Islove is a recording alias used by East Coast Canadian singer-songwriter Jeremy Francis Dollemont, who later released music as Francis Skyes. Born on Canada's east coast and based in Riverview, New Brunswick, Dollemont co-wrote and sang Glenn Morrison's dance hit Goodbye, the exact Islove credit in the Northern Dial library.

Toronto-based Canadian hip-hop artist J Shiltz is known for introspective, punchline-driven writing over jazzy, boom-bap production. His catalogue stretches from the 2011 album What I Stand For through later solo work and collaborations with artists including Junia-T, Rel McCoy and members of Monolith.
Toronto rapper and R&B artist J-Soul emerged from the city's west end and signed with Cash Money Records after building momentum around melodic records including Slow Wine and Toronto Plaza Hotel.

Toronto hip-hop and spoken-word artist J-Wyze, born Jelani Nias, has worked as an MC, writer, broadcaster and arts facilitator across the city's independent scene. His catalogue includes Proverbs and Herbs and later WyzeArt releases, with collaborations and production connections spanning artists including Motion, Rich Kidd, Saukrates and Kolor Brown.

Jaclyn Gee is a Vancouver hip-hop and R&B artist whose catalogue includes the 2015 album Gypsy Rose and collaborations with Canadian rappers including Snak the Ripper, Merkules and Eternia. Northern Dial carries Jaclyn Gee as part of British Columbia's independent hip-hop and soul scene.

Jacob Vallen is a Canadian music producer and independent artist whose work spans beat-making, production and collaborative recording. His professional profile identifies him as a producer from Canada working with artists remotely and across genres. Northern Dial carries Jacob Vallen as part of its Canadian producer catalogue.
Montréal-born Canadian producer Jacques Greene, the project of Philippe Aubin-Dionne, makes emotionally rich electronic music shaped by house, R&B and club culture.

Jamaican-born Canadian reggae singer Jah'Mila is a Halifax-based artist whose roots reggae incorporates soul and jazz. Her debut album Roots Girl won East Coast recognition and earned a Juno nomination, and her career has included performances and collaborations with Symphony Nova Scotia, the National Arts Centre Orchestra and the Toronto Symphony Orchestra.

Jahmar Carter is a Toronto-based producer and artist also known as Daxz and Lil DarkLord. As Daxz, he became known for production work connected to Drake's Grammy-nominated Back to Back and has worked with artists including KILLY, The Weeknd and Travis Scott. His co-credit with Shog Stan and WondaGurl on the 2026 single Girlfriend Pioneer Prodigy Veteran is his Northern Dial library credit.

James is the split Northern Dial credit for Canadian singer-songwriter Rob James, one half of Winnipeg pop and R&B duo McMaster & James with Luke McMaster. The duo's gold-selling Canadian run produced radio hits including Thank You, the exact James credit represented in the Northern Dial library.

Japandroids were the Vancouver duo of guitarist-vocalist Brian King and drummer-vocalist David Prowse, who met as students at the University of Victoria and formed the band after both settled in Vancouver. Working with only guitar, drums and two voices, they built an outsized sound around volume, repetition and songs about friendship, escape and the urgency of being young. Their 2009 debut Post-Nothing broke the duo outside Vancouver, with "Young Hearts Spark Fire" becoming an enduring statement of the band's all-in approach.

Celebration Rock in 2012 turned that momentum into an international breakthrough. Its eight songs refined Japandroids' combination of punk economy and arena-sized emotion, taking the band from small rooms to major festivals, late-night television and eventually a headlining show at Massey Hall. The duo expanded its arrangements and storytelling on Near to the Wild Heart of Life in 2017 without abandoning the direct guitar-and-drums chemistry that had defined the project.

After nearly two decades together, Japandroids announced Fate & Alcohol as their fourth and final studio album, releasing it in 2024 as a deliberate closing chapter. Their place in Canadian indie rock rests on how much scale they created from such limited instrumentation: two Vancouver musicians turned the energy of DIY rooms into communal rock songs that travelled internationally while remaining rooted in the emotional directness of the Canadian bands that first inspired them.

Toronto-born Canadian-Indian producer Jaspunit Sandhu, known as Jay Trak, built his career from local rap production into major Punjabi collaborations, first breaking through with Pengz and TwoTwo's Griselda Blanco.

Jaye Woods is the stage name of Mississauga-raised, Hamilton-based hip-hop artist, producer and therapist Jordan Heywood. Active since 2011 and formerly recording as Orijin, he blends rap, melody and reflective writing around healing, sensitivity and community, with provincial tours and a Canadian Music Week appearance among his credits.

JayTrillz is a Brampton hip-hop artist whose music reflects the Toronto and Brampton scene around him. He built his catalogue through independent singles and projects including Trillion Dollar Dreams, while speaking openly about the opportunities and challenges facing artists in the local music ecosystem. Northern Dial carries JayTrillz as part of its contemporary Greater Toronto Area rap catalogue.
Toronto-born rapper Jazz Cartier, born Jahmarie Adams, is known for theatrical, bass-heavy hip-hop and projects that earned Polaris Music Prize recognition and a Juno Award.

Toronto rapper JB is a Canadian hip-hop artist raised in Flemingdon Park whose independent career spans more than two decades. He earned MuchMusic Video Award nominations for Fire in Ya Eyes featuring The Game and Move Ya Body featuring Ghetto Flex, while his 2009 album My Environment documented the Toronto scene through collaborations with Dru, Michie Mee, Maestro and others.

Acadian singer-songwriter Jean-François Breau was born in Ontario and raised in Tracadie-Sheila, New Brunswick, building a francophone career through solo records, musical theatre and the Canadian group Salebarbes.

Montréal-born Jean-Pierre Ferland was one of Québec's defining singer-songwriters, writing hundreds of songs across a six-decade career and helping modernize francophone pop with landmark records including Jaune.

Jed Harper is a Newmarket-born, Toronto-based DJ and producer whose career spans hip-hop, house and club music. Formerly known as DJ Jedi, he became a fixture in Toronto nightlife, served as the Toronto Blue Jays' official DJ and performed at major festivals and clubs in Canada and abroad. Northern Dial carries Jed Harper as part of its Canadian DJ and electronic music catalogue.

Prince Edward Island-born, Halifax-based singer-songwriter Jenn Grant has built one of Atlantic Canada's most enduring modern folk-pop careers, using an airy, expressive voice to connect singer-songwriter intimacy with orchestral pop, Americana and the collaborative culture of the East Coast scene. Albums including Echoes and Honeymoon Punch brought her wider national attention, while The Beautiful Wild earned JUNO nominations and helped establish Grant beyond the regional awards circuit. Her writing has remained closely tied to place, family memory and emotional detail even as the arrangements around it have shifted from luminous folk-pop to country and atmospheric studio work.

Compostela expanded that reputation and was followed by Paradise and Love, Inevitable, records that continued Grant's relationship with producer and longtime collaborator Daniel Ledwell. Across the period she accumulated three JUNO nominations, multiple East Coast Music Awards and a Polaris Music Prize long-listing. Her 2023 project Champagne Problems widened the frame through collaboration, bringing together 13 Canadian musicians including Bahamas, Dan Mangan, Basia Bulat and Kevin Drew. The project helped earn Grant the 2024 ECMA for Songwriter of the Year, while "Judy," her collaboration with Kim Harris, received Song of the Year recognition.

Grant's 2026 album Queen of the Strait draws directly on childhood crossings between Prince Edward Island and the mainland and turns family history into a broader meditation on loss, survival and belonging. Co-produced with Joshua Van Tassel and Ledwell, the record moves deeper into country and Americana without severing the dreamlike quality associated with her earlier work. That continuity helps explain Grant's place in Canadian music: she has sustained a national career from Atlantic Canada while repeatedly drawing other Canadian artists into the work, making collaboration, geography and personal storytelling central parts of the same catalogue.

Jeremy Dutcher is a Wolastoqiyik singer, composer, pianist, ethnomusicologist and Two-Spirit song carrier from Neqotkuk in New Brunswick. Classically trained as a tenor, he began the project that became his debut album by studying century-old wax-cylinder recordings of Wolastoqey ancestors held at the Canadian Museum of History. Rather than treating the archive as static documentation, he brought those voices into new piano-led compositions and sang the resulting work entirely in Wolastoqey.

That 2018 debut, Wolastoqiyik Lintuwakonawa, tied contemporary composition directly to language revitalization and won both the Polaris Music Prize and the JUNO Award for Indigenous Music Album of the Year. Dutcher's second album, Motewolonuwok, widened the musical vocabulary through jazz, classical and pop elements and included English alongside Wolastoqey. It won the 2024 Polaris Music Prize, making Dutcher the first artist to win the award twice.

Dutcher's significance goes beyond awards. His work places endangered-language revitalization, archival recovery, queer Indigenous identity and contemporary composition inside the same artistic practice, refusing a separation between preservation and experimentation. That approach has led to orchestral collaborations, international performance and a broader public role in conversations about language, Indigeneity and cultural continuity.
